stemMd: Which pair can form an acid-base buffer in water?

options.label: A
options.textMd: A weak acid and its conjugate base

options.label: C
options.textMd: Two gases that do not dissolve or react

options.label: D
options.textMd: A strong acid and more of the same strong acid

options.label: E
options.textMd: Pure water and an inert insoluble solid

explanationMd: A buffer contains appreciable amounts of a weak acid and its conjugate base, or the corresponding weak-base pair. The base component consumes added acid, while the acid component consumes added base. A neutral salt alone lacks these complementary reserves.

distractorRationale.d: This does not provide a substantial conjugate acid-base pair capable of buffering.
distractorRationale.e: This does not provide the required acid-base reserve.
distractorRationale.c: They do not establish a useful aqueous buffer pair.
distractorRationale.b: A neutral salt of a strong acid and strong base is not a buffer by itself.
